prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one high-fidelity, professional desktop UI concept screenshot for OliveStudio, a modular PixiJS 2D game editor for macOS. Wide landscape 16:10 composition, edge-to-edge single app window, no monitor hardware, no perspective, no presentation board or comparison collage. Sharp, legible typography, precise spacing, consistent thin icons, realistic implementable interface. Main design problem: dozens of feature panels currently crowd the toolbar. Solve through hierarchy and progressive disclosure; never show a long row of module icons. Show the same project "Lumenwood", a painterly atmospheric 2D forest platformer scene with a small luminous creature, mossy platforms, fireflies, muted teal foliage, warm gold light. Canvas is actual game artwork, UI surrounds it. Selected object "Firefly emitter" with a subtle selection outline and small transform gizmo. Keep game scene sophisticated and controls highly readable. App name exactly "OliveStudio". No promotional slogans, no external captions, no watermark. This is a mockup, not code. DESIGN A: CANVAS FIRST. Inspired by the restraint and canvas-first interaction of Procreate, reinterpreted for a desktop game editor rather than copied. Graphite near-black surfaces, subtle olive/sage green accent, restrained 10px radii. Canvas occupies about 85 percent of window. Slim 52px top bar: macOS traffic lights, OliveStudio / Lumenwood breadcrumb left; centrally compact Play, Pause, Step icon controls; right "Tools" button and settings icon. NO permanent left sidebar. A small floating left rail of just four obvious icons for select, move, rotate, scale. One compact floating right Properties card, width roughly 260px, shows Firefly emitter, count 180, lifetime 1.4s, two color swatches, blend Add, compact sliders. A single small rounded bottom-centered workspace strip has only Scene, Animate, Effects, Logic modes; Scene selected. Bottom left a collapsed "Library" shelf with a small image icon; bottom right subtle zoom 100%. Show a compact open Tools popover at upper right with search and ONLY five labeled categories: Build, Scene, Motion, Audio, Automate; this is the unified entry to all less-used modules, no giant list. Generous negative space, no timeline or asset grid open. Premium minimal calm, the game canvas remains dominant.

DESIGN B: TASK WORKSPACES. A polished professional creative tool with fixed stable geometry and task-based workspaces, clean warm off-white/ivory chrome, charcoal text, thin neutral dividers and sage green active accents, no glass. Slim top bar shows OliveStudio / Lumenwood left, central workspace tabs "Design", "Animate", "Develop" with Animate selected; small Play icons and "Export" right. One narrow left sidebar 195px: Scene heading and ONLY six hierarchical objects Ground, Trees, Hero, Firefly emitter selected, Camera, Ambient sound; below a collapsed Library row. Large center stage. One right inspector 250px with heading Firefly emitter and neat parameter form count180 lifetime1.4s glowtexture blendAdd; sections collapsed for Spawn and Motion. A bottom timeline restricted to this Animate workspace: about 190px tall, track labels left with Hero and Firefly emitter, clear time ruler 0s to 5s and precise keyframes, playhead at1.2s. No secondary top row of feature icons. A small top-left nine-dot launcher labeled Tools exposes remaining modules without adding permanent panels, closed in this view. Clear hierarchy, readable compact density, subtle corners, well-aligned controls. This concept should clearly look like a disciplined task-based workspace, not floating canvas-first cards. Show stage occupies most remaining space.

DESIGN C: CONTEXTUAL STUDIO. Distinct architectural approach: compact charcoal background with cool gray surfaces, subtle muted lavender accent, modern flat tool UI. A very narrow 64px left primary navigation rail with ONLY five large coherent icon+small-label entries Scene, Library, Motion, Logic, Tools; Scene active. Short top header with project breadcrumb "Lumenwood / Forest entrance", central scene/Preview segmented switch, right Play and Export. Massive center canvas. NO left hierarchy sidebar, NO permanent bottom timeline. A small scene breadcrumb in the bottom left of canvas. On the right, one integrated drawer roughly300px wide with tabs "Object", "Effects", "History", Effects selected. Heading "Firefly emitter", large live particle preview inside subtle checkerboard field, four compact effect preset chips Fire, Smoke, Snow, Glow, and two clean controls Count180 and Lifetime1.4s, collapsed sections Appearance and Movement, bottom Apply button. The right drawer is the ONLY current contextual panel; no separate inspector or second particle panel. A bottom compact asset shelf only 115px high is pulled up, with a Library header, search, folder breadcrumb Forest / Effects and four small file thumbnails in a single row. Right drawer and bottom shelf have obvious collapse handles. A unified search field in header says "Find tools or commands" with shortcut glyph. Premium editorial spacing and professional tool ergonomics, subtle 6px radii, no marketing cards. Show a real usable restrained editor with all advanced tools behind the Tools launcher. Different composition and interaction model from both canvas-first and workspace tabs.
